# Change log

What changed in each Dédalo v7 release, newest first. Every change is filed under
who it affects — **users** of the application, **administrators** who install and
run it, and **developers** who build on its API. A release that needs something
from you when you update says so first, in an *Action needed* box.

Each release's *Wire contract* list names the deliberate changes to the API's wire
shape by the id under which the source tree records each one
(`engineering/wire_contract/`).

## Unreleased

Merged since the last release; these ship with the next one.

### For administrators

#### Fixed

- **The official Docker image now carries its signature in every registry that publishes it**

    The 7.0.0-beta.7 image reached GitHub Container Registry and Docker Hub without its
    signature, so `cosign verify` (and the installer's Official check) refused it there. The
    release process now signs the image in each registry it publishes to, with the same
    official identity, and a release already published unsigned is signed in place when its
    signature can be proven from the build. Verify an image as described in
    [Checking the signature](./install/docker.md#checking-the-signature).

## 7.0.0-beta.7 — 2026-10-25

278 commits: `git log --no-merges v7.0.0-beta.6..v7.0.0-beta.7`

!!! warning "Action needed when you update"

    - Dédalo prereleases are now published releases — from 7.0.0-beta.7 on, each beta is a fixed, signed version you can install and update.
    - The Docker and Trial installer installs the image of its own release — `7.0.0-beta.7` for a beta — and a stack built from an earlier beta needs `--skip-version-check` once on its next image update.

### For users

#### Security

- **The change history of a password field no longer shows the stored password hash.**

    The *Value* column of a record's change history showed, for each past change of a password field,
    the stored (encrypted) password itself, to administrators and to any user allowed to read that
    field. It now shows the mask `****************`, as the field does everywhere else. Restoring a
    past password from the Time Machine is unchanged.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-09-30-password-hash-never-served`.

#### Removed

- **The hidden 'Calm Scholarly' design preview is removed.**

    Dédalo carried a second, optional interface design that only a developer could
    reach, by adding `?design_preview=1` to an address or by setting one browser
    value. It was a temporary vehicle for a redesign, and that work is now part of
    the standard interface.

    The preview is gone: the design switch in the menu, the startup script that
    applied it, and the second palette behind it. Nothing changes for a user who
    never opted in. A user who did opt in returns to the standard design, and their
    browser keeps a setting that no longer has any effect.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-19-design-line-removed`.

#### Changed

- **Image quality selector now appears only on hover or on an active component; touch screens keep it visible.**

    Before, the quality chip ("1.5MB ▴▾") sat permanently on top of the image in the edit view, overlaying the picture's top-right corner. Now it stays hidden while the component rests: it appears when the pointer is over the component, when the component is active (clicked), or when it takes keyboard focus, and it fades back out.

    The chip is still keyboard-reachable (it keeps its place in the tab order, and focusing it reveals it), and at rest it no longer intercepts clicks in that corner of the image. On touch screens — which have no hover — the chip keeps working as before, always visible.

    Applies to the edit view of `component_image` only.

- **Opening a rich-text field no longer downloads the editor on the first click.**

    Clicking into a description, transcription or any other rich-text field used to
    start the download and parsing of the editor itself, so the first click sat
    there for a moment before the cursor appeared.

    The editor's engine is now fetched in the background while the edit form
    settles — once per page, only when the form actually shows an editable
    rich-text field — and the first click only creates the editor for that field.
    Fields are still not loaded until used, so a form with many text areas does not
    carry one editor per field. On a metered connection (browser "data saver") the
    background fetch is skipped.

- **CSV import guesses the target section from more file names and remembers your correction.**

    In the *Import Dédalo CSV* tool, the target section tipo is now read from any word of the file name that has the tipo shape, so names such as `export_Mint_07-10-2026-numisdata6-raw.csv` resolve to `numisdata6` instead of `raw`. When a name holds several tipos, the field offers them as suggestions.

    A section tipo typed by hand is remembered in your browser for that file name and comes back after a reload, marked *remembered*; click the mark to forget it. Nothing is stored on the server.

- **The Import files tool's options panel reads as three clear blocks, and the import button stays in reach.**

    The panel at the top of **Tools → Import files** spread five groups of different heights
    and widths across the bare page, each label on its own line height, so the options read as
    unrelated fields. It is now one card above the file queue, in three columns: what the files
    go into (Processor, Target field and Quality, stacked), *Replace existing files*, and *New
    files*. Each option is a label above its own control, and each group heading has room under
    it. When the tool is narrower than three columns allow (below 1024 px wide, or in a narrow
    window), the columns become one, in that same order.

    The **Import** button used to sit far below the last field, off screen on a long queue. It
    now stays in a bar along the bottom of the tool while you scroll.

- **The inspector's Data box keeps its size when you select another component, and you can resize it.**

    Before, the inspector rebuilt the component information each time you selected a
    component. The Data box briefly collapsed, then grew or shrank to fit that
    component's value, which moved Project, Relations and Latest changes up and down.

    Now the Data box has a fixed height of 10rem whatever the value. Drag its bottom-right
    corner to make it taller or shorter: the height is kept across reloads. Double-click
    the box to fit it to its content for a moment. The Copy button sits in the Data
    header, so you can reach it without scrolling, and it also works when a value is too
    large to display. An empty value now reads "Empty".

- **A relation table is framed, with no rules between its column titles**

    The column titles of a relation table sat in a box each, so every pair of
    neighbours drew two vertical rules between them and the titles read as a grid of
    sealed cells. Those boxes stopped at the header too, leaving the left rule
    hanging above the rows.

    The titles are labels, not fields, so the rules between them are gone. The
    table's own edges carry the frame instead: one rule down each side, from the
    titles to the last row, plus the line above the titles. No column moves.

- **Time machine tool list on phone renders as one card per version**

    The time machine list (tool_time_machine) on small screens no longer stacks
    every field of every version into one unbounded run of label/value rows. Each
    version now renders as a distinct bordered card with its ID header on top, the
    restore icon takes the tool colour, and fields the snapshot does not carry are
    hidden (they remain visible in the desktop table).

- **On a phone, the time machine marks the picked version across the whole row and brings its preview into view.**

    Two things got in the way of reading a long history on a phone.

    The picked version is marked in orange, but only the value half of its Id row was filled,
    so pale strips of card showed at either side of the mark and the row read as a loose chip
    rather than the row you are on. The mark now runs the full width of the row, Id label
    included.

    And picking a version deep in the list left what you picked out of sight above you: the
    preview of the chosen version and the **Apply and save** button both sat over the fold.
    Picking a version now scrolls its preview to the top of the tool, just under its header,
    so the version you are about to restore is the first thing you see.

- **On a phone, the time machine's two version panels, its Apply action and its page counter now stack into one readable column.**

    The time machine band at the top of the tool compared the live version and the chosen
    snapshot in two half-width columns. On a phone that left the value hugging the left
    edge with an empty half beside it, floated the **Apply and save** button up into the
    version labels, and wrapped the page counter's chevrons onto a line of their own.

    Now every block gets the full width: the live value first, the chosen snapshot under
    it, then the actions. Each version is announced by a strip above its value — *Now* for
    the live one, the snapshot's date and time for the chosen one. The still-empty snapshot
    panel stays out of the way until a version is picked, **Apply and save** takes a row of
    its own, and the page counter keeps its chevrons on one line. On a desktop nothing
    changes.

- **Checkboxes and radio buttons fill with a deeper orange so the white tick shows in every browser**

    A ticked checkbox or a picked radio button no longer depends on which browser you
    use. The checked fill was the bright brand orange, and each browser picks the
    tick's colour from it: Chrome and Edge drew a near-black tick, Firefox and Safari
    a white one, so the same box disagreed from one browser to the next.

    The checked fill is now a deeper Dédalo orange (`#db760f`), dark enough that every
    browser draws the tick — and the radio dot — in **white**, and it clears the 3:1
    contrast floor a checked control needs to read as checked. The app's own drawn
    boxes in the dark theme take the same white tick. Unchecked boxes, focus rings and
    the rest of the bright accent are unchanged.

- **The date field's calendar now writes the dates the catalogue actually stores — including year-only, year+month and BCE (negative) years — with localized month names and full keyboard and touch support.**

    Before: clicking the calendar opened a third-party picker that only understood complete CE dates in a four-digit year (it also showed English month names regardless of the interface language). Opening it on a year-only, year+month or BCE value fell back to *today*, and picking a day there replaced the value with a full modern date.

    Now: the calendar is built into the component and speaks the same date model the catalogue stores. The year field accepts any signed year (with a CE/BCE toggle and decade steps), the month and weekday names follow the interface language, and the footer commits the precision you need — the bare year (`-205`), the year and month (`04/2022`) or a full day. The picker is fully keyboard driven (arrows, PageUp/PageDown, Home/End, Escape; the calendar button is a tab stop, and Alt+ArrowDown opens it from the field; pressing the calendar button again closes the open calendar instead of reopening it), its touch targets grow on phones and tablets, and it follows the light and dark themes. In the search panel the calendar button appears on the field's top-left corner when the field takes focus, a range's two dates share the row in full and its `<>` hangs under the gap between them, so the card keeps the same height as every other search field. The separate clock picker now uses the operating system's own time wheels on touch devices, and its button closes it on a second press too.

#### Added

- **The profile permission tree can be filtered by name or tipo.**

    A profile's **Access and permissions** tree lists the whole ontology, and a node
    several levels down (a component inside a section inside an area) was hard to
    find: you had to open the branches one by one.

    The tree now has a search box above it. Typing part of a node's **name** or its
    **tipo** keeps that node together with the path to it, and opens the branches on
    the way down, so the permission radios are in front of you instead of hidden.

    - Matching ignores case and accents (`administracion` finds `Administración`).
    - Several words must all match the same node (`user name`, not one each).
    - Matching nodes are highlighted in yellow, so a result is easy to spot among the
      open branches that lead to it.
    - The counter shows how many nodes match; a very broad query renders the first
      500 matches and says so — type more to narrow it.
    - The filter only changes what is *shown*. Permission values, and the propagation
      of a checkbox or a global `x / r / rw` radio, still apply to every node,
      visible or not. Clearing the box restores the tree exactly as you had it.
    - Jumping to a section from **Latest changes** clears the filter: that jump exists
      to show you the section, and a query could hide it.

- **The address bar now names the open record, so an edit page can be copied and reopened**

    While editing a record, the address bar now carries its id (`?tipo=…&mode=edit&id=…`),
    so copying the URL and opening it later — or in another tab — lands on **that** record.
    Before, the URL only named the section, and reopening it showed whatever record the
    browser's stored edit position happened to point at.

    The same URL is also the reliable form for a bug report or an assistant prompt: it
    identifies the section and the record without the search that produced them.

    Alongside it, two long-standing traps around pasted record links are gone: a link that
    named a record could come up with an empty form ("no records found") when the browser
    had a stored edit position, and leaving such a page for the list could show a list of
    one. The list itself is unchanged, and paginating inside an edit page still works; a
    reloaded or shared record link simply shows that record, one at a time.

- **The image vector editor now supports undo and redo**

    Cmd+Z (Ctrl+Z on Windows) undoes the last change in the image vector editor, and
    Shift+Cmd+Z / Ctrl+Shift+Z (Ctrl+Y on Windows) redoes it. Drawing, moving or
    resizing a shape, deleting, colour changes, moving the raster image, resetting
    the raster and adding/deleting layers are covered. Layer visibility, layer names,
    the colour swatch and zoom are editor settings and are not part of the history.
    See [component_image](./core/components/component_image.md).

- **The inspector shows again who created, last modified and published a record, and when.**

    In edit mode, the inspector's *Information* panel always showed `-` for *Created* and
    *Modified* and `Never` for *Published*. It now shows the date and user of each, and for
    publication the first and last time the record was published. If the record was later
    withdrawn from publication, the panel says so. The values load just after the record
    appears, so opening a record is not slower.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-19-inspector-record-info`.

- **Export: columns are added and reordered by tap on a phone**

    The **Export** tool built its column list by dragging: a field dragged from the
    available-fields list onto the *Active elements* list to add a column, and a
    selected column dragged up or down to reorder it. A finger cannot drag, so on a
    phone neither could be done at all — the tool opened, but its columns could not
    be chosen.

    On a touch screen each field in the available-fields list now carries a **+**
    that adds it as a column on a tap, and every selected column carries **up / down**
    buttons and a **✕** that move or remove it. Both do exactly what the drag did (a
    field already added is pointed at rather than duplicated). On a computer nothing
    changes: the drag is still the gesture there.

    The phone view is also straightened out around that. The fields list fills the
    whole width (it shared its row with the other, empty drill column), the empty
    column list names the gesture it has (it points at the **+** instead of saying
    "drag a field here"), the **+**, the remove **✕** and the option checkboxes are
    full 44px tap targets, the export preview fills its panel, and the result area no
    longer reserves a blank half-screen before any export is run.

    The **Export presets** editor (and its Search twin) opens as the full-width
    sheet on a phone — maximum room for the form — while staying the small card on a
    computer. And a saved preset is one tidy line in the panel on a phone — the
    apply ring, the name, then Edit and Delete — instead of the desktop columns
    squeezed to slivers with their labels stacked one letter per line.

- **On a phone, a drilled search field level shows its path**

    In the search **Fields** list, drilling into a link field (a portal) opens the target
    section as a new level. On a phone each level replaces the previous one, so the list
    header now shows where you are: the section path, e.g. `People / Projects`, instead of
    only the current section name. When the path is too long for the header it is shortened
    on the **left** (`… / Level two / Projects`), so the deepest — most relevant — terms stay
    readable. On a desktop, where the levels stay side by side, the header is unchanged.

- **On a phone, moving between search field levels now slides**

    In the search **Fields** list, opening a link field (a portal) to reach a deeper section —
    or returning with the level's `×` — now animates: the incoming level slides in from the
    side it comes from (right when drilling in, left when going back) instead of the list
    swapping with no motion. It makes it clear that you are moving between levels of the field
    selector, not replacing its contents. Desktop (side-by-side levels) is unchanged.

#### Fixed

- **The autocomplete result list no longer opens as a blank band**

    An autocomplete field painted its dropdown the moment the search answered, but
    before the matched records had been built: every result was an empty row. On a
    slow render the open list became a tall blank panel over the form, with rows
    appearing one by one — which read as broken layout.

    Rows are now appended only once their record is rendered, in result order, and
    the picker answers only when the whole list is ready: the open list is either
    empty or complete, never a band of blank rows. A row that fails to render is
    skipped and named in the console instead of leaving another blank band. The fix
    is in `core/services/service_autocomplete/js/view_default_autocomplete.js`.

- **component_iri edit row lays out on one aligned line**

    The component_iri edit row mixed wrapped widths (30% + 20% + 50% plus the active checkbox forced an overflow) so the label, title and url fields scattered across misaligned lines. The three now share one line with stable proportions when the container is wide, and wrap to neat full-width lines when it is not. The active checkbox also joins the component's hide-at-rest rule: it is only visible on hover, on the active component or on keyboard focus. Checkbox and remove/link icons render inside one flow cluster at the row end (content_actions) that wraps with the row, so the icons no longer overlay the inputs on narrow, wrapped rows.

- **A read-only field's value starts under its own label again**

    When a text field is not editable — a view-only user, a Time Machine preview, a
    print view — its value sat about half a character to the left of the label above
    it, while an editable field's value sat exactly on it. The two looked like two
    different grids in the same record.

    The value now starts on the same left inset as its label, editable or not. The
    alignment covers every single-line field that renders as plain text (text,
    number, date, e-mail, URL), not just the one that was reported.

- **Rich-text fields in a language with no bundled editor translation now open in English instead of not opening at all.**

    The editor that backs the `html_text` view ships a UI translation only for some
    languages (70 of the 138 application languages). For the rest — Georgian,
    Welsh, Icelandic, Tamil and others — the editor refused to start, so those
    fields could not be opened or edited at all.

    The editor now falls back to its English interface when its translation file is
    not available; the field opens and works as usual. Content and data language are
    unaffected.

- **Change history no longer fails, and restore no longer writes a broken value, when an old history entry holds a malformed link value.**

    Opening the history of a linked field (for example a user's profile in the inspector's
    *Component history*) could answer with an unexpected error, and no entry at all was shown, when one
    very old history entry stored the value in a shape earlier versions used (a bare record number
    instead of a link). The history now opens: every well-formed entry shows as usual, and an entry
    whose stored value cannot be read as a link is shown empty instead (the response flags it with the
    reason, for developers). The same entry previews empty in the Time Machine tool, and restoring it
    (the field alone, the whole record, or a deleted record) is refused with a message saying the entry is in an old format, instead of writing the broken value
    into the record (before, the restore stored it and the field showed nothing usable). The current
    value stays as it is. The stored history itself is not changed.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-24-tm-malformed-relation-cell`.

- **Image derivatives are encoded at full quality again — sharper web and list images, and somewhat larger files**

    Every generated image size (`1.5MB`, `6MB`, `thumb`, the alternative-format
    twins) was compressed at quality 82, a value inherited from the first version of
    this engine. The previous engine encoded images at **90**, and inspection of the
    same picture side by side shows the difference plainly: the web size looked
    softer and smoothed-over, most visibly on fine texture and lettering.

    Derived images are now encoded at 90 again, matching the previous engine. Expect
    the `1.5MB` and other jpg sizes to grow by roughly 40–75 % for the same pixel
    dimensions (on the reference record, 55,988 → 97,453 bytes); thumbnails grow
    much less. The `original` quality's viewable copy was already written at 100 and
    is unchanged.

    Nothing is rebuilt automatically: existing records keep their current files until
    a master is uploaded again or the record is regenerated from the media versions
    tool (**Regenerate files** after deleting the size you want rebuilt).

- **Deleting an image's last file now clears its vector drawing, so a new upload starts fresh**

    Deleting every quality of an image used to remove the rendered SVG overlay but
    keep the vector layers in the record; uploading a new image afterwards showed the
    old shapes over the new picture. The delete that removes the last file now clears
    the stored layers too. The cleared drawing is kept in the Time Machine, so the
    previous version can be recovered. See
    [component_image](./core/components/component_image.md).

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-08-09-image-svg-envelope-preserved`.

- **An image uploaded in a format the browser cannot show (TIFF, PSD, PNG…) keeps its full-resolution original AND regains the viewable copy, so the "original" quality is selectable again**

    Dédalo stores an image in tiers, and the best one is the `original`. Uploading a
    `.tif` (or `.psd`, or any format a browser cannot draw) left that tier holding
    only the file you uploaded: the engine indexed it and let you download it, but
    it had no picture to show. The image component's quality selector only lists
    tiers that hold the type's standard format (`jpg`), so the `original` quality
    disappeared from the selector altogether, and the media-versions panel's preview
    cell for it stayed empty.

    The original tier now also carries the standard-format copy beside your upload —
    `rsc29_rsc170_1.tif` and `rsc29_rsc170_1.jpg` side by side, the pair Dédalo has
    always stored. The copy is made when the file is uploaded into `original` or
    `modified` (including a colleague's retouched master), and it is what every
    reader resolves when it picks a tier's picture: the quality selector, the media
    versions panel, list and mosaic views.

    Your uploaded file is never modified or replaced, and the copy is only a viewable
    companion: every derived size is still built from the original file itself. It
    is encoded at maximum quality (not the lighter web compression), so a large scan
    keeps its detail when you open the `original` tier.

    Records uploaded before this fix heal with one **Regenerate files** click in the
    media versions tool (or the next cache update sweep).

    One visible consequence of restoring the established behaviour: a media export
    or download that asks for the `original` quality of such a record now gives the
    viewable `.jpg` copy (the standard format), not the raw `.tif`. The raw file
    remains listed and downloadable as its own version in the media versions panel.

- **The propagate tool on a Project filter now offers the same options as the component.**

    Opening *Propagate component data* on a **Project** (filter) component showed the selector empty — no checkbox, so nothing could be propagated. The tool's editable panel is a throwaway copy of the component that is saved once before it renders, and the server's answer to that save carried the component's value but not its option list (the projects you are authorized to use). Only the Project filter family was affected: selects, radio buttons and the rest kept their options.

    The server now answers every save of a filter component with the same options its edit view offers — the propagate tool panel, the record edit after a save, and the staged forms all show the project tree as before.

- **An image's drawing envelope is removed with the record's last file, not with one quality**

    Every image is displayed through a small SVG envelope that wraps the record's
    web-quality picture. Removing the record's files never removed that envelope, so
    with every quality deleted the editor kept loading a wrapper whose picture was
    gone and the browser painted its broken-image icon — in the edit view and in the
    media versions panel.

    The envelope now follows the record's files, with the same rule the files
    themselves follow: it is moved to a `deleted` folder (recoverable, exactly like a
    deleted quality file) **only when the record has no file left in any quality** —
    no original, no retouched master, no web size, no thumbnail, no alternative
    format. Deleting one quality, even the web size, leaves the envelope where it is,
    because the record still holds a picture.

    A record emptied before this fix keeps its leftover envelope until it is
    regenerated: one **Regenerate files** click in the media versions tool clears it,
    and the record then shows the normal empty placeholder.

- **Turning pages in *Latest changes* no longer fails with a permission error for users who are not administrators.**

    A user allowed to see a section's change history could open the inspector's *Latest changes*,
    but moving to the next page of the list answered with a permission error. History lists are
    read-only, so they no longer take part in field locking at all, and paging through them works for
    every user the profile allows.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-23-own-lock-cleanup-ungated`.

- **The image vector editor now deletes shapes and layers reliably**

    Deleting a selected shape with Delete/Backspace did nothing when several shapes
    were selected or when focus was on the image-quality selector. Deleting a vector
    layer could leave it in the saved drawing, and the raster layer's trash button
    could duplicate its contents. Delete now works for single and multiple selections
    from the quality selector, the base photograph cannot be deleted by accident, a
    deleted layer is removed from the saved drawing, and the raster trash empties the
    annotations while keeping the photograph. See
    [component_image](./core/components/component_image.md).

- **Saving a drawing in the image vector editor keeps the image visible**

    Clicking save in the image vector editor no longer replaces the picture with a
    broken-image placeholder. The drawing was saved correctly all along; only the
    editor's live view lost the image until the record was reloaded. Switching the
    image quality now also keeps working on images that carry a vector drawing.

- **The acquisition tools no longer start an import while a new Preview is loading**

    In the auction-catalogue and journal acquisition tools, clicking **Preview** again
    left the previous review on screen, with its **Confirm import** still enabled,
    until the new preview arrived. An import started in that moment was then hidden by
    the new review, and the new review's **Confirm import** could start a second import
    beside the first. The previous review now disappears as soon as you click
    **Preview**, and **Confirm import** does nothing while a preview is loading.

- **Remove background works again in the image rotation tool.**

    **Remove background** failed every time, with a bare `Worker error` in the panel and
    nothing else. Three faults sat behind it, all client-side: the worker was requested
    at a path one directory above the application root, so the browser never loaded it;
    the model it asked for (`briaai/RMBG-1.4`) is not loadable by the bundled
    Transformers.js runtime; and the model's output shape had changed under it, so even
    a successful run would have thrown instead of returning the cut-out.

    It now measures the subject with `onnx-community/ISNet-ONNX`, the same DIS/IS-Net
    family as before, and any failure reports its actual reason (missing model file, no
    WebGPU, worker error) instead of a blank banner. A failed run no longer claims
    "Background removal completed" and no longer leaves the button disabled.

    **Administrators:** the weights come from the install's own model store — never a
    CDN — so a store seeded before today has to add
    `onnx-community/ISNet-ONNX` (176 MB fp32: `config.json`,
    `preprocessor_config.json`, `onnx/model.onnx`) to `<private>/ai_models/`. Until it
    is there the tool says so plainly instead of hanging.

- **Unpublishing every record of an RDF, XML or Markdown publication now also removes its combined file and ZIP**

    An RDF, XML or Markdown publication writes one file per record. It also writes a
    combined document (RDF and XML only) and a ZIP archive, both built from the records
    the run published. If a run published nothing, for example because every record in
    it had been unpublished, the run removed the per-record files but kept the combined
    document and the ZIP from the previous run. Those files still held the unpublished
    records, so anyone could still download them from the public files directory. The
    run still reported that it had completed. Now a run that publishes no records
    removes the previous combined document and ZIP as well.

- **A refused side panel no longer takes over the whole page.**

    When a part of the page that a user may not open — for example a history block in the
    inspector — was refused, the whole page switched to the "You don't have permission to access
    this page" panel and stayed there: every other block showed the same panel and navigating
    elsewhere did not recover. The refusal now stays inside the part that was refused, the rest of
    the page keeps working, and moving to another section clears a page-level refusal. See
    [errors](./core/system/errors.md).

- **The References panel and its graph open for every user who can read the record, and their page counts add up**

    A user who was not the superuser got *Insufficient permissions* when opening a
    record's References panel or its relations graph, even with read access to the
    record. They now open for anyone who can read the record, listing only the
    referring records that user may see. The total shown by the panel's paginator
    now matches its pages: before, a user who could not see some referring records
    got short pages and could never reach the total, and counting those records grew
    slower with every record the user could not see. See
    [relation_list](./core/ontology/relation_list.md).

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-22-related-search-one-scope`.

- **Users who are allowed to see a section's change history can open *Latest changes* and *Component history* again.**

    A user who is not an administrator but whose profile grants a section's history list got a
    permission error in the inspector's *Latest changes* and *Component history*. The history now opens for every user the profile allows, also when the
    history list sits inside a group of the section. Users without that permission no longer see the
    two blocks at all, and a block that cannot load shows one short line inside the block instead of a
    full-page error. The record counter of a history list follows the same permission.
    The history follows the same rule as the Time Machine tool: a user allowed to see a section's
    history sees the changes of every record of that section, also of records outside their projects
    and of deleted records.
    A history list shows only the section it was opened for, for every user: a search of another
    section remembered in the session no longer replaces it after a reload. An administrator's own
    Time Machine list, opened with no section, keeps its saved search across a reload.
    The history never shows the past values of a field the user's profile does not let them read on
    the record: those cells stay empty, the rest of the change (who, when, which field) is shown.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-22-tm-scope-whole-request`.

- **The acquisition tools no longer let you start a second import while the first one's outcome is unknown**

    In the auction-catalogue and journal acquisition tools, **Confirm import** stays
    disabled while the server has not said what an import did. Three ways around that
    could still start a second import beside the first:

    - Running **Preview** again replaced the review, including its disabled **Confirm**,
      with a new one you could click. **Preview** is now disabled until the import's
      outcome is known, or until you choose to try again.
    - An import that ended without saying what it did turned **Confirm** back on by
      itself. That happens when the server process running it stopped, when it was
      stopped partway, or when the server could no longer find it. The panel now shows
      the server's own message, asks you to check the records, and turns **Confirm**
      back on only when you say so.
    - **Check my jobs** offered "It did not start: allow a new attempt" even when it
      listed an import of the same kind that had just finished, which might be the one
      you started. You now open that import first to see what it did. When no import of
      that kind is running or finished recently, the button now says only that, and
      leaves the decision to you.

- **The acquisition tools no longer go silent when a job's progress is lost, and the move panels show a refused run.**

    In the auction-catalogue and journal acquisition tools, if the connection that
    reports a preview's or an import's progress dropped before the job finished, the
    panel showed nothing more and re-enabled its button, although the job could still be
    running on the server. Clicking again could start a second import beside the first.
    The panel now says that it lost the job's status and that the job may still be
    running, keeps the button disabled, and offers **Check again**, which reconnects to
    the same job.

    In the auction-catalogue tool's company picker, a slow first search for the auction
    house could answer after a newer search you had typed, and replace your choice of
    Entity with the old one. Only the latest search now counts. A search that fails is
    shown as an error, not as "no candidates" with *Create new Entity* already selected.
    **Confirm** also waits until the Entity is chosen, so an import never drops the
    auction's company link without telling you.

    In the maintenance move panels (move TLD, language, locators, to portal, to table),
    a run the server refused, for example because of a bad option, used to show nothing
    in the panel. The panel now shows the reason, the server's own sentence, and the
    request id.

    For developers: with `SHOW_DEBUG` on, the browser console's request line now lists
    only the names of a request's options and hides their values. Before, it hid only
    some secret keys and printed the login password.

- **The acquisition tools show why a preview or an import failed, instead of "Done."**

    In the auction-catalogue and journal acquisition tools, a preview or an import that
    failed on the server was reported as "Done.", and the panel then stopped responding
    for that run. Pasting a URL the tool does not support, a page that could not be
    read, or an import the server refused all looked like a success.

    The panel now shows the reason, in your language, with the server's own sentence
    when it says more — for example *Only OAI-PMH journal/repository URLs are supported
    right now.* If your session expired while the job was running, the login window
    opens. A job you stopped is no longer reported as done either: the panel says it
    ended without a result.

    The per-record lines of an import summary state their failures the same way.

    In the maintenance move panels (move TLD, language, locators, to portal, to table),
    when two previews of the same files run at once, only the latest one can now reveal
    the Execute button. Before, an older clean preview could reveal it after your newer
    preview had failed.

- **The selected field is fully tinted in a light orange — its list surfaces included — and its label stays readable in both themes.**

    When you clicked a field, only its label turned orange: the tint behind the component was
    `#fffaf5`, 1.02:1 on the light card — invisible, so an active field looked much like an
    inactive one.

    The active field now paints the palette's orange field tint on the whole component (label
    and value): a light cream, `#fff7ef`, in the light theme and a warm brown, `#4a3424`, in
    dark, following the theme a reader has chosen. The search panel's highlight of a field
    with a value uses the same tint, which is lighter than before (it was `#fce8d2`). Text you
    select is not painted in this tint: a selection has its own colour, which stands out
    against it (see the entry on selected text).

    The label on that tint is the palette's deep orange — 5.6:1 in both themes. The bright
    Dédalo orange it was painted with before is a *fill* colour: on the tint it measures
    2.3:1, which is why the header of a selected Date or Text field was hard to read.

    Nothing paints a slab of its own over that tint any more. A portal's list draws a card —
    white in light, near-black in dark — for its rows to sit on, and each row carries a grey
    remove column; both sat as boxes in the middle of the lit field. Inside a selected field
    those surfaces no longer paint, at every depth, so a portal nested in a row behaves like
    the one holding it, and an empty portal reads as the fields around it. The rows, their
    columns and every control keep their place: only the paint goes, so nothing moves.

- **A record restored from an archive no longer shows the history of a deleted record that had the same id.**

    Restoring an archive re-creates each record with the id it had when it was archived. If
    this installation once held a different record with that id, deleted since, the restored
    record's history used to list that deleted record's changes as if they were its own, and
    they could be restored onto it. A restored record's history now starts with the restore,
    as it already did for records imported with an explicit id. The deleted record's history
    is kept.

- **The assistant's find-or-create no longer duplicates a record under concurrent calls**

    When two assistant requests asked for the same record at the same moment (find it by its fields, or create it), both could miss it and both create it, leaving two records with the same identity. The search is now asked again under a lock before anything is created, so the second request finds the record the first one created.

- **The "Report a problem" tab only appears for users whose profile grants the error-report tool.**

    An administrator whose profile does not include **Error report** still saw the purple "Report a problem" tab on the right edge; clicking it only answered "The tool is not active or not authorized for your user".

    The server now tells the page whether the tool is granted (no extra request), and the tab shows only then, so it appears exactly for the users who can use it: those whose profile includes the tool, and the superuser. To give an administrator the tab, add **Error report** to their profile's tools.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-21-error-report-granted`.

- **Stopping a background export now stops it at once, even while its record selection is still being computed.**

    Pressing Stop on a background export used to wait until the database had finished computing
    the export's whole record selection — on a large selection, minutes in which the export kept a
    database connection busy for nothing. Now Stop (and the export lane's deadline, and a server
    restart) interrupts that computation in the database itself: the export ends as stopped
    straight away and its connection is freed.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-11-export-buffered-cap-and-admission`.

- **The acquisition tools and move panels no longer re-enable an action when the server did not confirm whether the job started.**

    In the auction-catalogue and journal acquisition tools, a preview or an import
    whose start the server never confirmed (the request timed out, the connection
    dropped, or the server answered that the same request was still in progress or
    its outcome was unknown) used to re-enable **Confirm** as if it had been refused.
    Clicking again could start a second import beside the first. The panel now says
    the job may be running and keeps the button disabled. **Check my jobs** lists your
    jobs of this kind: **Show this job** follows the one that started, and a new attempt
    is offered only when none of them is running or queued.

    The action buttons are now truly disabled while a job runs, so the keyboard can no
    longer start the same job twice. A job status that falls silent, or stops halfway
    through, is declared lost after 15 seconds, with **Check again** to reconnect to the
    same job.

    In the maintenance move panels (move TLD, language, locators, to portal, to table),
    a run whose start the server did not confirm is no longer shown as refused: the
    panel says it may have started and asks you to check before running it again.

- **Pasting into the search panel's Id field adds to what is already there instead of replacing it.**

    In the search panel, pasting into a section's *Id* field replaced the whole field with the
    clipboard, so ids you had already typed were lost, and a single pasted line went in
    unfiltered, letters included.

    A paste now goes where the cursor is, or replaces only the selected text, like a paste
    anywhere else. A single line keeps only the characters the field accepts (digits and the
    search operators `.` `,` `>` `<` `=`). A list pasted from a spreadsheet column, one id per
    line, still becomes a comma-separated list, and a comma is added between it and the ids
    already on either side.

- **The reference picker of a text area separates the term and its thesaurus part (… | …), instead of gluing them.**

    In the reference picker of a text area, a term whose record carries no ancestor chain showed the thesaurus part glued to it (`LatinaAgrupador`). The picker now separates the columns that actually render, so the same entry reads `Latina | Agrupador`, like the rest of the list.

- **A text area reference can link the same term from several references, and deleting a reused reference keeps the others linked.**

    In the reference picker of a text area, giving a second reference a term that another reference already used was refused as a duplicate, yet the reference was still written into the text, pointing at a link the database never saved. The same term can now be linked from any number of references.

    Opening an existing reference (or draw tag) showed an empty *New tag* field instead of its current term, and pressing *Apply* there deleted the link of the reference. The picker now shows the current term, and *Apply* without changes keeps it.

    Reusing a reference (the *Reuse tag* list) is also clearer and safer: each entry shows its tag number and an icon, selecting one shows its term in the *New tag* field, and deleting or moving one of several text fragments that share a reused reference no longer unlinks the term the other fragments still point at. A reused reference also takes the label of the reference it reuses.

    Draw tags: *Apply* in the draw tag picker saves the chosen term again (it failed before), and *Delete* no longer fails on a record without draw links.

- **Update cache never overwrites an edit saved while it runs**

    *Update cache* regenerates a field by saving its current value again. It used to read each
    record once, at the start of that record's turn, and save that copy later, possibly
    minutes later when a media field of the same record was rebuilt first. A change someone
    saved to the field in between was silently replaced by the old value, and a record deleted
    in between was brought back. Now each field is read and saved again in one step, with the
    record locked, so a change saved meanwhile is kept and a deleted record stays deleted. A
    record that stays locked by someone else is skipped and listed, and a re-save the system
    refuses is listed instead of being counted as done.
    A record whose stored value the system refuses to save again (for example an old value in
    a shape the field no longer accepts) is now listed and left untouched, and the run goes on
    with the next record: it used to stop the whole run at that record.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-21-update-cache-locked-resave`.

- **Translatable fields in tool forms show the value in your data language, not always in Spanish**

    Some forms build their fields by asking the server for each field's definition — the
    Hierarchy tool's *Name*, for example. When that request named no language, the server
    answered Spanish, so a record holding *Unofficial toponymy* in English and
    *Toponimia no oficial* in Spanish showed the Spanish value to a user working in English,
    and an edit there was saved into the Spanish value.

    Those fields now use your current data language, as every other field does.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-20-element-context-default-lang`.

- **Clicking a field puts the cursor in it, every time**

    Clicking into an Email or Number field while another field was selected
    sometimes selected the field but left no cursor in it: typing went nowhere
    until you clicked a second time. The same happened to Date, IRI and colour
    fields, and when moving into a field with the Tab key from a related-records
    list.

    Now the click or the Tab always leaves the cursor where you aimed it. Clicking
    the second value of a field no longer sends the cursor back to the first one, and clicking the label or the empty space of the selected
    field puts the cursor back in its first box. Lists of related records, check
    boxes, radio buttons and text editors keep their own behaviour, and the buttons
    of a field act as before.

- **Turning a list page no longer jumps the layout**

    Every paginated list (section lists, portals, the inspector's *Latest changes*
    and *Component history*) replaced its rows instantly, and the new page is often
    a different height: a value that took one line on one page takes six on the
    next. The block snapped to the new height in one frame, so the page content
    below it jumped — on a phone, the whole form under your finger.

    The rows container now grows or shrinks over the page turn (200 ms, the same
    motion as the rest of the interface), and it is clipped while it does, so no row
    paints over the paginator. Users who ask their system for reduced motion get the
    instant swap instead. The paginator's own dim is deferred too: a fast page turn
    no longer blinks the arrows, and a slow one still fades.

- **Search: the drag-a-field slot is the same height as the field cards beside it**

    The search panel's third slot (**Drag a field here**) was taller or shorter than
    the field cards next to it, so a row of filters looked ragged. Every card in a
    row now takes the row's height: the tallest field card, or the drop slot, sets it
    for all of them. A drop slot alone on a row still matches a field card. Its **+** and the one on
    **Add group** are the light outlined glyph, not the filled disc.

- **Thesaurus lists are sorted by name in the reader's language.**

    The installer's *Thesauri* step and the *Add hierarchy* maintenance panel now list thesauri in the same order: alphabetically by their name in your language, with accents ignored, inside each typology group. Before, the installer sorted by code, so *Spain* (`es`) appeared between *Eritrea* and *Ethiopia*, and the panel used a third order that put accented names after Z.

- **Selected text is visibly highlighted in every field, active or not**

    Dragging over the text of a field used to paint the range in the same pale
    orange as the surface behind it — exactly the tint of the field you had just
    activated, and nearly the white of every other field. You could not tell
    whether the text was selected.

    A selection now paints as a clear amber slab with dark ink (11.8:1) in the
    light theme, and as a stronger warm brown with white ink (5.1:1) in dark. It
    reads clearly against the active field's tint and against the plain card, in
    inputs and text editors alike.

- **Opening a record by link no longer lands on a one-row list.**

    A link that names a record — `?tipo=<section>&section_id=<id>`, which is what the
    inspector's **Local Ontology** pen, a list row's edit button and a job's record
    link all produce — used to open the record as a **list of one**: the columns of the
    section list, no edit form, no inspector. It now opens the record for editing, as
    it did before the engine rewrite.

    The cause was on the server: the first-boot request (`start`) received the record
    id but described the page element in *list* mode, and the page then inherited that
    mode into its own data request. A section link that carries a record id is now
    always answered in **edit** mode, whatever mode the link asks for. Links to a
    component or an area keep the mode they ask for.

- **Inspector history panels read as blocks on a phone or tablet**

    Below the desktop break the inspector drops its rail and renders inline, where
    *Latest changes* and *Component history* kept a narrow multi-column table shape
    designed for the side panel. The column labels were squeezed into 15px-wide
    strips (one letter per line) and the values were pushed out of their cells.

    Each history entry is now one block: the date (orange) and author on the first
    line, what changed next, and the snapshot value last, separated by a hairline.
    The desktop side panel is unchanged.

- **The Section id search field fills its card like every other search field.**

    In the search panel, the *Id* field of a section rendered its value box at its content width: the box stayed short and left dead space inside the card, while every other field's box spanned the card. It now fills the card like the rest, in both the empty and the valued (highlighted) state.

- **Orange warning buttons are readable — white text on a deeper orange in the light theme.**

    Warning buttons were painted in the bright brand orange, with dark text. White text on
    that orange measured 2.44:1, under the readable minimum, so it could not be used.

    Warning buttons now use the same orange as the warning messages: white text and icon on a
    deeper orange in the light theme (4.62:1), near-black on a bright orange in the dark theme
    (6.76:1). Hovering deepens the colour and keeps the text readable (5.21:1 light, 7.86:1
    dark). The section toolbar's warning buttons, transparent until you hover them, light up in
    the same colours.

- **Dark mode: the page canvas no longer sits above the cards, and empty-field hints are legible**

    In **dark mode**, the page background was painted with the light theme's canvas
    grey. Because the dark palette inverts the grey ramp, that grey became *lighter*
    than every content surface: cards, the list body and the login card sank into a
    lighter field, and the search band around the filters merged with it. The canvas
    is now the role token meant for it, which is darker than every surface in dark
    mode and the same colour as before in light mode — the light theme renders
    byte-for-byte identically.

    Empty-field hints — a portal or dataframe's empty value (*Etiqueta*, *Título*,
    *http://*, the date *DD/MM/YYYY* masking), and the browser's own placeholder in
    every other input — were below the WCAG AA floor: 1.9:1 in light and 2.7:1 in
    dark for the portal hint, 3.1–3.9:1 for the rest, because the browser paints a
    placeholder with its own light-scheme grey and the app never themed it. Hints now
    carry the muted-text token in both themes: 8.1:1 on the dark card and 5.7:1 on
    the light one.

    The edit view's field placeholders were also dimmed by an extra 30% opacity that
    took them under AA; they now render at their label ink's own contrast.

- **Tool Export — the presets panel no longer shows a blank band between its header and the presets.**

    The Export tool's presets panel kept an empty pagination block (39px of blank
    space) between the "Export presets" header and the first row, and between the
    header and the "no presets" message on an empty list. The collapsed paginator
    now takes no space; a preset list long enough to paginate still renders its
    pagination.

- **Plain-text filter values join terms with ', ' when the section map defines no separator**

    component_filter in the 'text' list view smashed its selected terms together
    when the section context supplied no `fields_separator` ("MIB
    AntigüedadBibliografíaMIB medieval-moderno"). An absent separator now falls
    back to ', '; a separator the context does define — empty included — is
    respected as before.

- **List headers stay readable in Safari, even when rows have different heights**

    In Safari, after paging through a list whose rows have different heights (for example the interviews list, with its identifying images and information widgets), the column headers could collapse into a thin, clipped strip and the first rows below them were hard to read. The header cells no longer let Safari recompute the header height from the data rows after a page change, so paging, sorting and late-loading widgets leave the header intact in every page.

    No action is needed on update.

- **The line under a list row is unbroken across empty columns**

    A list row draws its separator as a 1px line under each cell. A cell that held no
    value was given a zero width, so it painted no line: in a relation table the
    separator stopped where the record's first empty column began, and the row read as
    if it ended there.

    An empty cell now keeps the width of its column, so the line continues to the end
    of the row. No column moves: the column widths come from the grid, not from the
    cells.

- **Mosaic hover: the record id is no longer cut off, and the publication switch is centred**

    Hovering a mosaic tile in edit mode shows a small overlay on its top-left corner:
    the record id with its pen, and — in portals that carry one — the publication
    switch on the other side. Two things were wrong there.

    The id chip was a fixed cell, narrower than an id of five or more digits, so the
    leading digits of the number were cut off by the tile's edge: `104299` read
    `04299`. The chip is now as wide as the id it holds, so the number is whole.

    The publication switch sat slightly left of and above the middle of its cell.
    Its value is centred in the cell now, so the switch rides the tile's corner
    evenly, and the id chip's own drag handle stays where it was: a band under the
    chip, revealed when you hover it.

    Nothing else moved: tile size, the record's image, the pen, the switch's colours
    and every other control are the same.

- **A portal row's edit cell now fills the row, like its trash cell.**

    Hovering a row of a portal list — a component like *Autoridad*, or *Monedas* —
    lit two cells: the id cell turned green behind the number and its pen, the last
    cell turned red behind the trash. They were not the same box. The red covered the
    row's whole height; the green stopped at the icon's own height, leaving a strip of
    untouched row under it — more of the row on a two-line value, most of it on a tall
    media row.

    Both cells are the row's height now, so a row reads as one band and the pen and
    the trash are equally easy to hit. The number and its pen hold the row's first
    line, level with the trash icon at the other end, so a row still reads along a
    single line. Nothing else moved: rows, columns, their widths, the height a row
    takes and every other control are the same.

- **The date field's calendar button is a full-size tap target and no longer covers the field label**

    On a touch screen the date field's small round calendar button — the one that opens the date picker — sat on top of the field's own label (for example *Fecha de captación*), so part of the label was hidden behind it, and the button itself was too small to tap reliably.

    On a phone the button now sits inside the field row, at the end of the date box, at the size of the app's other touch targets. The label and the date value are fully readable, and the button is easy to hit.

- **The Import files tool's options panel lines up on a phone**

    The panel at the top of **Tools → Import files** — Processor, Target field, Quality, and the matching / new-files switches — was laid out for a wide window. On a phone its labels and their drop-downs landed at different left edges, the drop-downs ran off the right edge of the screen, the section headings were centred over left-aligned content, and each switch caption sat a full space away from its own switch.

    On a phone the panel is now one option per row: the label sits above its drop-down, every drop-down spans the full width and starts at the same left edge, the headings read left like the rows beneath them, and each switch row is a full-height tap target with its caption beside its switch. The suffix-to-field legend ("- A -> Obverse") drops to its own full-width line instead of squeezing in beside its caption. On a wider screen the panel is the three-block card described in its own entry.

- **Ontology and thesaurus search: the result highlight and the loading state are now in sync.**

    Searching in the Ontology and Thesaurus areas showed a confusing sequence: the
    loading state ended before the results were highlighted, so the page looked
    finished and only afterwards the matched term popped in and the page scrolled,
    sometimes re-centering even when the term was already on screen.

    Now the whole sequence is one coherent transition: the loading dim lasts until
    the matched terms are highlighted, the page scrolls only when the first match
    is out of view (and never shifts sideways without need), a brief pulse marks
    the highlighted term even when no scroll happens, and the search panel's Apply
    button shows a busy state while the search runs.

- **Search on a phone: the fields panel's level header is as easy to tap as the fields themselves**

    The **Search** panel's fields list lets you drill into a related section, and the grey
    band at the top of the list names the level you are in ("People / Projects") and
    carries the **×** that takes you back out of it. On a phone that band was about a
    third shorter than the field rows under it, so the × was the smallest thing on
    screen — a thumb aimed at it usually missed, and the way back out of a level was
    easy to lose.

    The band is now the same height as the field rows, and the × has a full-height tap
    target of its own at the end of it — the same target the rows give their **+** — so
    closing a level is as easy as adding a field. The group bands between the rows
    ("Identification"…) take the same height, so the whole list is one rhythm. On a
    computer nothing changes.

- **On a phone, the section list buttons and their show/hide arrow no longer overlap or jump around.**

    The list toolbar of every section has a small arrow that shows or hides the row of
    action buttons (New, Delete, Tools). On a phone the action row used to wrap onto its own
    line and push that arrow onto a **third** line, alone and stuck to the left edge, while
    the collapsed state kept it on the right of the search row — so the arrow jumped across
    the screen as the row was shown or hidden.

    Now the arrow keeps the right edge of the search row in both states, the action buttons
    keep their own full row underneath, and the arrow is a normal (no longer rotated) button
    that is big enough to tap comfortably. On a desktop nothing changes.

    Screen readers also get the state of that button (`aria-expanded`) and the region it
    controls (`aria-controls`), which they did not before.

- **Tools on a phone use the phone's own spacing and header height; only part of the phone adjustments were reaching the screen.**

    Every tool panel carries a set of adjustments for small screens: tighter page padding, a shorter header, a smaller tool name. Half of them did not reach the browser — the shared stylesheet declared them *before* the styles they were meant to override, so the desktop values won and each tool kept its desktop padding and header height on a phone. The result was a panel whose content started lower and whose header (which stays pinned while you scroll) took more of the screen than it was designed to.

    The panel now uses the phone measurements throughout: the body keeps a half-rem gutter instead of a full one, the header is a little shorter, the tool name sits at the phone size, and the header's controls band still spans the full width with its bottom edge flush with the header. Desktop layouts are unchanged.

- **The Update cache tool reads properly on a phone: one component per row, its options and model under it, all lined up.**

    On a phone, **Update cache** squeezed three columns (component · regeneration options · model/tipo) into 360–600px. The component name wrapped over two or three lines, the long model names spilled past the right edge of the panel, and the column headings no longer sat above the columns they name — so the list read as a ragged staircase and the tap row for a component was about 30px tall.

    A phone now shows one component per row: the checkbox and its name on a 44px tap row, the model/tipo as a small subtitle under it, and any regeneration option (e.g. *delete normalized files*) as the last line of the row. Every secondary line hangs under the name's text, and the group headings keep only the group name, since the two column captions describe a layout a phone no longer has.

    The same three columns also line up with their headings again on wide screens: a column is now sized by the whole list rather than by each row separately, so the headings and the values beneath them cannot drift apart, and no model name is cut off or broken mid-word.

- **Upload buttons keep a clear gap between their icon and their label on a phone**

    On a narrow screen the icon inside a labelled button was pushed to within two pixels of its text, so the button read as *⤒Start upload* with the glyph touching the word — and the gap looked uneven from one button to the next, because one icon's drawing fills its box and another's does not.

    The upload tools' buttons (**Add files**, **Start upload**, **Cancel upload**, **Delete file**, and the same controls on each queued file) now keep the same icon-to-label spacing they have on a wide screen, so the icon reads as a separate mark before the word and the buttons line up as one set.

- **Each file in the upload queue is a card, so you can see where one file ends and the next begins**

    In the upload queue (**Tools → Import files**, and the MARC 21 and Zotero importers) each file's thumbnail, name, option menus and buttons ran straight into the next file's, with nothing between them — on a phone the list read as one long column and it was easy to lose which name, which menu and which Delete button belonged to which file.

    Every file is now a bordered card: a white panel with a rounded border and a gap before the next one. A file's start and end are unmistakable, and its menus and buttons sit inside its own card.

- **Uploaded-file rows stack on a phone instead of running off the side**

    The file rows in **Tools → Import files** (and in the MARC 21 and Zotero importers, which use the same upload widget) were laid out as a single desktop row — a thumbnail, the filename, the file's two option menus and its Start / Cancel / Delete controls side by side. On a phone that row is wider than the screen, so the part past the right edge was simply not there: the row's menus and its Delete and Cancel controls could not be reached at all, and a long filename was squeezed into a column so narrow it broke one letter per line.

    Each uploaded file now takes its own block on a phone: the thumbnail, then the filename and size, then the file's option menus full width, then its controls, one under the other. Nothing runs off the side, and every control is on screen.

- **The upload queue's "select all" checkbox says what it does again**

    Above the list of files waiting to be uploaded there is a checkbox that ticks every file's Delete box at once. It had lost its caption, so it showed as a bare square with nothing to say what it selected — easy to miss and easy to misread.

    The checkbox carries its label again — **All** (in the interface language) — and the label is part of the control, so tapping the word ticks the box just like tapping the box itself. Each file's own Delete checkbox is unchanged.

- **The search panel keeps the values you typed when the page reloads.**

    The search panel saves what you are building as you go, so a reload brings it back. That
    automatic save could store only the fields of the search and drop their values: after a
    reload the panel showed the right fields, all empty, and the search had to be typed again.
    This happened when the panel's working copy carried the *save values* switch set to *No*,
    a switch that belongs to named presets and cannot be changed on that working copy.

    The automatic save now always keeps the values. The *save values* switch still decides,
    as before, whether a named preset you save stores its values or only its fields (a
    template).

- **The autocomplete options panel no longer clips its section list**

    In a search or edit field that offers an autocomplete, the gear panel that lists
    the searchable sections (and the related-record filters) laid its options out as a
    two-column table. A long section name such as *Tipologías de ontología* or
    *Causas de restauración* made that table wider than the panel itself, so the
    right-hand column was cut off at the panel edge: some sections were half-visible
    and, because the overflow was hidden rather than scrollable, some checkboxes could
    not be reached to deselect them one by one.

    The list is now a grid that fits the space it is given. It shows a single readable
    column on a narrow field and two or more columns once there is room for whole
    names, so no option is clipped and the panel stays inside its card.

- **Search option tooltips are legible in dark mode.**

    Hovering a search field showed the "Search options" help tooltip as a
    bright, near-white panel against the dark interface. It now follows the
    theme like every other floating panel: a dark elevated card with a subtle
    border in dark mode, a light card in light mode.

- **The Tools menu in a section list opens its tools again on a phone.**

    On a phone or any touch screen, opening **Tools** in a section list showed the menu, but tapping a tool in it (Export, Import, Diffusion, Update cache…) did nothing: the menu closed and no tool opened.

    The menu was dismissed by the first touch of the tap, before the tap had reached the row; on a touch screen that left the press landing on the list behind the menu instead of on the tool. It now closes on the same press that opens the tool, so a finger works as the mouse and the keyboard already did.

### For administrators

#### Security

- **Names and values typed by one user can no longer run script in another user's browser**

    Several places in the work interface inserted a stored value into the page as
    markup instead of text: the name of an image annotation layer in its
    **Delete** confirmation, the field labels of a saved or shared search preset,
    the record terms and field values in the graph view's node panel, the
    selected record's title in the autocomplete choice grid, the people offered by
    the transcription tool's **Assign speakers** dialog, and the user and record
    names listed by the **Lock components** maintenance panel. A value containing
    markup — for example a layer named `<img src=x onerror=…>` — ran as script for
    any other user who opened it. These values are now always shown as plain text,
    and the same rule now holds for every label, count and message the interface
    builds around a value: a confirmation dialog's title and its question, for
    example, are always text.
    Two internal lookups keyed by text a user controls (URL parameters and the
    autocomplete search cache) were also hardened so such a key cannot alter them.
    No action is needed on update.

- **Server hardening from the CodeQL review — the tag-badge address refuses over-long requests, rich text keeps only raster-image `data:` links, and literal `&lt;` text is no longer turned into `<`.**

    - The address that draws the small tag badges in transcriptions (`…/component_text_area/tag/?id=…`)
      needs no login, and a long run of `<` in it made the server spend over a second of processing per
      request. Such an address (longer than 4096 characters, far beyond any real tag) is now refused
      with a `400` before it is read, and the tag clean-up itself runs in linear time — as do the
      other places that strip markup from text (search ordering, publication values, thesaurus empty
      checks, list previews, subtitle files, external-record markup, image annotation envelopes,
      merged RDF publications).
    - Rich text keeps a `data:` link in an attribute only when it is a raster image (PNG, JPEG, GIF,
      WebP, AVIF, BMP). Any other `data:` link — an SVG image, XML, plain text — is replaced by `#` when
      the text is saved. Descriptive attributes (`alt`, `title`, …) are not affected, so an alternative
      text that starts with "Data:" is kept.
    - Text in which a cataloguer literally typed `&lt;` is now shown, counted and indexed as `&lt;`,
      not as `<`: the indexation grid, the transcription character count, the semantic index and the
      import code lookup decode each entity once. The numeric spellings of the five special characters
      (`&#60;`, `&#x27;`, …) are decoded there too, exactly as the previous engine did.
    - Two small file races are closed: the update log and the media access markers are created in one
      step that never empties an existing file, and the staged upload name is size-checked and read
      through the same open file.

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-25-tag-id-length-cap`, `WC-2026-10-25-rich-text-data-url-raster-only`.

- **Third-party packages updated to their latest stable releases, closing every known advisory against them.**

    The engine and the publication packages (the v2 publication API, the site builder and
    the publication-host agent) now install with no known security advisory, measured
    against the public advisory feed at release time. Twenty-one advisories are closed:
    `body-parser`, `qs`, `undici`, `fast-uri`, `serialize-javascript`, `hono`,
    `ip-address`, `vite` and `zod` move to their fixed releases, and `nodemailer`, which
    sends Dédalo's mail, moves to 10.2.1.

    Other notable moves in this release:

    - **zod 4.6.7**, the validation library, is now the only copy in every package.
    - **Anthropic SDK 1.3.0** (was 0.131) for the Dédalo assistant. It speaks the newer
      API version 2026-10-21 and sends the API key in the `Authorization` header
      instead of `X-Api-Key`. Nothing changes for an installation that reaches the
      Anthropic API directly. If outbound traffic goes through a proxy or gateway that
      reads `X-Api-Key`, make it read `Authorization` instead.
    - **Swagger UI 5.34.0** (was 5.33.1) and **Scalar API reference 1.76.0** (was 1.72.4)
      on the v2 publication API's documentation pages. The legacy v1 API's Swagger page
      moves from 5.32.14 to the same 5.34.0 (see
      [vendored library versions](./development/vendored_library_versions.md)).
    - **OpenTUI 0.6.8** (was 0.6.1), the terminal installer's interface library.
    - **Biome 2.6.3** (was 2.5.15), the code checker. Nothing changes for an
      installation; this only affects development checks.
    - **actions/upload-artifact 7.0.2**, in the release and CI workflows.

    The Bun runtime pin stays at 1.4.3.

- **SQL the engine runs through psql no longer appears on the psql command line**

    Several maintenance and installation doors (ontology import and export, ontology
    update snapshots, thesaurus export, the restore door, the installer's probes and
    the seed compiler) passed their SQL to `psql` as a command-line argument. Any
    local user could read those statements in the process list while they ran, and on
    Linux a statement over 128 KiB failed to start at all (`E2BIG`). The SQL now
    reaches `psql` on its standard input; the command line carries only connection
    and output options. The terminal installer's host-preparation plan keeps its
    short catalog probes on the command line, where its Review shows them.

- **A user can only assign a record to projects they belong to**

    The *Projects* field lists only the projects the logged user belongs to, but the
    server used to store any project it was sent. A modified or out-of-date request
    could therefore place a record in a project the user is not a member of, or, on
    a user's own *Projects* field, grant a project the editor cannot see. Saving now
    refuses a project the user is not a member of with a message, and nothing is
    stored. Global administrators can still assign any project. Projects already on a
    record, including those added by colleagues in other projects, are never removed
    by this check. See [component_filter](./core/components/component_filter.md#security-model).

    Wire contract: `WC-2026-10-22-filter-project-pick-membership`.

- **Site builder: a Claude Code turn turns off its auto-updater and telemetry in every confinement mode, not only when confined**

    A site builder turn run by Claude Code now always starts the agent with its
    auto-updater and its non-essential traffic (telemetry, error reporting) switched
    off. Before, those two switches were applied only to a turn confined under its
    site identity: on an instance declared `AGENT_CONFINEMENT=none`, a Claude Code
    turn ran with the auto-updater on — which could replace the very binary the
    daemon had checked before the turn — and sent traffic to hosts the instance's
    plan does not name. opencode turns already had their equivalent switches in
    every mode. Nothing to configure.

- **Site builder: `provision remove` and `provision adopt` can no longer be hung by a pipe planted at a turn HOME's `.gitconfig`, a site's `site.json` or an instance marker**

    The site builder provisioner reads a few files that an agent or a site
    identity can write — a turn HOME's `.gitconfig` when an instance is removed, a
    site's `site.json` and the instance marker (`.dedalo_site_instance`) at the
    root of an install when it is adopted. A named pipe planted at any of those
    names made the root command wait forever. Those reads now open without waiting
    and read only a regular file; anything else is treated as unreadable (a marker
    that is not a regular file counts as no marker), which each command already
    reports. Regular files — including an operator's symlinked password file — are
    read as before.

- **Outbound fetches judge an IPv6 address through every NAT64 prefix that holds it, so nested prefixes cannot reach an internal address.**

    Before the server fetches a URL on a user's behalf, it judges an IPv6 address that carries
    an IPv4 address through NAT64 by that IPv4 address. NAT64 prefixes can sit one inside
    another: two translators, a name server answering with two addresses, or an outer and an
    inner prefix declared in `DEDALO_NAT64_PREFIXES`. The same address then carries a different
    IPv4 address through each, and the check read only the first prefix in its list. Depending
    on the order, an address could pass as a public site while, through the inner prefix the
    network actually routes by, it reached the cloud metadata endpoint.

    Now the address is read through every prefix that holds it, the most specific first, and it
    is refused if any of those readings is not a public address. Nothing to configure; the
    prefixes are declared as before (see
